title: Freddie Keppard's handkerchief over his valves
summary: Keppard hid his fingering from copyists and once blew a mute across a club floor; Cheatham found him loud and crude but good.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Now, you did hear Freddy Kephard?

Now they've always said about Freddy Kephard that he was so afraid people would -- other trumpet players would copy him and there's an old story that he used to play with a handkerchief over his valves so that --
That's right, so you wouldn't see what he was fingering.

That's a true story. One day in Chicago, the word got out that Freddy Kephard played -- was playing and he blew a note so loud that he -- that the straight mute that he was playing jumped clean out of his horn, went all away across the night club floor. He hit this note, and so naturally everybody went up there, all the musicians would go up to hear Freddy Kephard, to see him do it again. But he never did it again.
Did you ever talk to anyone who was there a -- that night?
Well, no, I only heard the rumor, it was a lot of musicians, everything that happend in Chicago

those days, you would hear it through the musicians. Everything that Louis did or anybody else did, you would hear from the musicians and naturally you go round to see who's doing it. What was happening. Yeah, that was the way Freddy was, he didn't want anybody to steal his ideas, so naturally he's covered up his fingering.
How did he compare to some of the others?

Well, you couldn't compare him with Louis Armstrong. I don't think he had the taste that Louis Armstrong had. (or Sheffner or Bob Sinnes) Red Allen. He wasn't as tasty as -- he was real crude, you know. But good.
And you had to hear him because he was very loud.
Very loud. But he wasn't as tasty as the rest of the guys.
